pattern: ADR P11 rule 2: the material answer is written as PMI, so it is no longer stored
evidence: ADR P11 rule 2 (src/feature_table.rs storable): a file stores only the answers that leave no PMI, and the file's PMI is the only copy of the rest. Every case's base answers (the oracle's meta.answers) include part.material = "steel"; the committed files (written before P11) store it, so their resume read-back is {"part.material":"steel"}, while today's writer writes the material as PMI (the part's existing read-back is unchanged: material steel) and stores nothing, so answers_for gives {}. Seen on every part of all 16 written cases (18 parts), and nothing else changes on the 14 cases other than NIST CTC-03 and CTC-05 (whose other changes have entries of their own). Found by tests/cross_engine.rs rust_written_files_match_the_current_presentation_writer, which compares today's write of the case (examples/write_fixtures.rs) with the committed rust.step.gz field by field ('python' is the committed file's read-back, 'rust' today's). The committed files and Python's read-back of them ((b), cross_engine.json) are deliberately not regenerated or recaptured for this; only this exact case and path are covered, and any other change still fails.

evidence: Maintainer decision D8 (commit d9067fb): one location dimension locates every hole on its located side and every other hole on the same line from the same reference, and the writer adds only the missing directions, never a second location. pattern: D1: an old intent keeps a planner general row only on a hole it sizes or locates
evidence: Decision D1 (commit 9717139, 'A general-tolerance answer writes only its note'): the writer's upgrade of an old intent without planner rows (dimensioning::upgrade) keeps a planner general row only on a hole the intent sizes or locates, or, off holes, where a general row of its kind touches the same faces.
